item.title: Diffusion in one paragraph
item.description: An image diffusion model learns one skill: given a noisy image, predict the noise in it. During training, it takes real images, adds a random amount of noise, and learns to predict exactly what was added. To draw something new, you start from pure noise. At each step the model predicts the noise, and a sampler uses that prediction to make the image a little cleaner. After 20 to 1,000 such steps an image appears. A text-to-image model also reads your prompt at every step, so the cleaned-up image matches the prompt. The terms below name each piece.

item.title: Inside a transformer block
item.description: A transformer turns a list of tokens into one vector per token, passes those vectors through a stack of identical blocks, and reads the next-token logits off the last one. The numbers on this page come from SmolLM2-135M, the small model several labs use: 30 blocks, vectors of 576 numbers, a vocabulary of 49,152 tokens.

item.title: ML in one page
item.description: A model is a function with millions of adjustable numbers. Training adjusts those numbers until the function gives useful answers. This page names each piece in the order training uses it.

item.title: Reading the numbers
item.description: The labs report attacks and defenses as measurements. This page explains every number they print, in the order you meet them. Most of the helpers live in labs/_shared/evalkit.

item.title: Sampling knobs
item.description: A language model writes one token at a time. At each position it scores every token in its vocabulary (the logits), and a decoding rule picks one. The knobs on this page are that rule’s settings. They change the reply without touching the weights.

item.title: Vectors without the math
item.description: Models store meaning as lists of numbers and compare them with a few simple operations. Every example on this page uses two or three numbers so you can check it by hand. Real models use hundreds or thousands, and the operations are the same.
